Setup Section:
Note, if you already went through the previous demos and have your prams samples in your environment, you do not need to do this,
but I am putting a simplified setup chunk for those that do not. 
```{r}
### 1. Setup ----
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

### 2. Load data ----
prams <- read_sas("phase8_arf_2016_2021.sas7bdat")

### 3. Construct IPV variable ----
ipvv <- c("PAB6HUS", "PAB_XHUS", "PAD6HUS", "PAD_XHUS")

prams_IPV <- prams %>%
  filter(complete.cases(across(all_of(ipvv)))) %>%        # remove missing IPV rows
  filter(!if_any(all_of(ipvv), ~ . %in% c("B","T"))) %>%  # remove blank/teen-mom codes
  mutate(IPV = if_else(
    PAB6HUS == 2 | PAB_XHUS == 2 | PAD6HUS == 2 | PAD_XHUS == 2,
    2, 1
  ))

### 4. Create 1:1 sample (1000 yes / 1000 no) ----
set.seed(456)
prams11_sample <- bind_rows(
  prams_IPV %>% filter(IPV == 2) %>% slice_sample(n = 1000),
  prams_IPV %>% filter(IPV == 1) %>% slice_sample(n = 1000)
)

### 5. Create 1:3 sample (1000 yes / 3000 no) ----
set.seed(123)
prams13_sample <- bind_rows(
  prams_IPV %>% filter(IPV == 2) %>% slice_sample(n = 1000),
  prams_IPV %>% filter(IPV == 1) %>% slice_sample(n = 3000)
)

### 6. Select final variables for modeling ----
vars_needed <- c(
  "YY4_DOB","HISPANIC","MAT_RACE_PU","MAT_AGE_PU","MARRIED","INSNONE","PP_NONE",
  "MAT_DEG","MAT_WIC","STRS_ARG","STRS_BIL","BPG_DEPRS8","MH_PGDX8","PGINTENT",
  "CIG_1TRI","CIG_2TRI","CIG_3TRI","CIG_PRIOR","OTH_TERM","MM_NOMD","TYP_INJR",
  "PRE_ABUS","PRE_MHDP","KOTELCHUCK","ASK_ABUS","ASK_DPRS","STATE","NEST_YR",
  "VITAMIN","IPV"
)

vars <- vars_needed[vars_needed %in% names(prams11_sample)]

prams11f <- prams11_sample[, vars]
prams13f <- prams13_sample[, vars]

```


1.3.3: Visualizations

1.3.3.1 First, let's look at maternal age from our large prams dataset via a histogram, it's just as simple as using the hist() function
```{r}
#histrogram
hist(prams$MAT_AGE_PU)
```


1.3.3.2 Now, lets go back to our subsetted data and get summary statistics for the maternal depression before and maternal depression after pregnancy variables 
```{r}
summary(prams11f$BPG_DEPRS8) #before
summary(prams11f$MH_PGDX8) #during
```


1.3.3.3 ggplot 2 is a package that can create many visually appealing and detailed graphs. Lets back a scatterplot for maternal age versus maternal weight gain for the state of North Dakota in 2020
```{r}
prams_nd2020 <- prams %>% 
  filter(STATE == "ND") %>% 
  filter(NEST_YR == "2020")


ggplot(data = prams_nd2020, aes(x=MAT_AGE_PU, y=MOMLBS)) +
  geom_point() 
#this geom_point is what makes it a scatterplot, you can use geom_bar, geom_line, and others to change chart type
```

1.3.3.4 Now, let's try creating the same plot but adding titles and axes labels
```{r}
#it's the same ggplot function, but color changes the color of the points, 
#alpha controls transparency
#and labs gives labels 
#finally we are adding a minimalist theme 
ggplot(prams_nd2020, aes(x = MAT_AGE_PU, y = MOMLBS)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "Maternal Age vs. Maternal Weight Gain (North Dakota, 2020)",
    x = "Maternal Age (years)",
    y = "Maternal Weight Gain (lbs)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
#notice how we build our base plot and then add layers
```
